slot.brief: A cyclic process on a P–V diagram; compute net work done in the cycle by comparing areas of expansion and compression strokes.

stem: An ideal gas undergoes a cyclic process $A \to B \to C \to A$. Path $A \to B$ is an isobaric expansion at $300\text{ kPa}$ from $2\text{ m}^3$ to $5\text{ m}^3$. Path $B \to C$ is a straight line on the $P$–$V$ diagram to the state $(100\text{ kPa},\ 2\text{ m}^3)$, and path $C \to A$ is an isochoric pressure increase back to the initial state. The net work done by the gas in one complete cycle is:

verdicts.working: A=(300 kPa, 2 m³), B=(300, 5), C=(100, 2). W_AB = 300×3 = 900 kJ; W_BC = ½(300+100)×(2−5) = −600 kJ; W_CA = 0. Net = 300 kJ, equal to clockwise triangle area ½×3 m³×200 kPa.

working:
The net work done during one cycle is given by the algebraic sum of the work done during each stroke:
$$W_{\text{net}} = W_{A \to B} + W_{B \to C} + W_{C \to A}$$

1. Expansion stroke ($A \to B$):
$$W_{A \to B} = P \Delta V = 300\text{ kPa} \times (5 - 2)\text{ m}^3 = 900\text{ kJ}$$

2. Compression stroke ($B \to C$):
The area under the line from $(5\text{ m}^3, 300\text{ kPa})$ to $(2\text{ m}^3, 100\text{ kPa})$ is a trapezium:
$$W_{B \to C} = -\left[\dfrac{300 + 100}{2}\text{ kPa}\right] \times (5 - 2)\text{ m}^3 = -(200\text{ kPa}) \times (3\text{ m}^3) = -600\text{ kJ}$$

3. Isochoric stroke ($C \to A$):
$$W_{C \to A} = 0$$

Thus, the net work done is:
$$W_{\text{net}} = 900\text{ kJ} - 600\text{ kJ} = 300\text{ kJ}$$

Alternatively, for a clockwise triangular cycle on a $P$–$V$ diagram, the net work equals the area enclosed:
$$W_{\text{net}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times (5 - 2)\text{ m}^3 \times (300 - 100)\text{ kPa} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 200 = 300\text{ kJ}$$

Independent check: A=(300 kPa, 2 m³), B=(300, 5), C=(100, 2). W_AB = 300×3 = 900 kJ; W_BC = ½(300+100)×(2−5) = −600 kJ; W_CA = 0. Net = 300 kJ, equal to clockwise triangle area ½×3 m³×200 kPa.
